Crispy Garlic Parmesan Chicken Wraps🍗🧀🌯 The flavours are absolutely phenomenal, one of the best wraps made using a sheet pan. Low effort, minimal cleanup and incredibly delicious🔥 Great to serve for large groups/gatherings at home Macros Per Wrap (10 Total) 423 Calories | 41g Protein | 25g Carbs | 18g Fat Ingredients (Makes 10 Wraps) Garlic Parmesan Chicken - 600g Raw Boneless Skinless Chicken Thighs, cut into cubes - 600g Raw Chicken Breast, cut into cubes - 2.5 Tsp Salt - 2 Tsp Chilli Flakes - 3 Tsp Parsley - 4 Tsp Italian Herbs - 3 Tsp Paprika - 4 Tsp Garlic Granules or Powder - 200g Grated Parmesan - 6 Tsp Olive Oil - Avocado Cooking Spray (use before baking) Garlic Pamesan Creamy Sauce - 350g Light Evaporated Milk - 2 Tsp Italian Herbs - 1 Tsp Garlic Powder - 1 Tsp Paprika - 80g Grated Parmesan - 100g Light Cream Cheese - 15g Light Butter Wraps & Filling - 10 Low Carb Wraps (Brand: Mission) - Shredded Lettuce - Chopped Tomatoes - Chopped Onions 👨‍🍳 Cooking Instructions 1. Slice chicken breast and thighs into cubes. Add seasonings with grated parmesan cheese and drizzle of olive oil. Mix until well coated. 2. In a pan on low heat, add light butter with seasonings. Toast for a minute before adding evaporated milk, extra Parmesan and cream cheese. Stir till smooth and creamy. 3. Line a sheet pan with parchment paper, spread marinated chicken evenly (do not overcrowd), add light layer of cooking spray then bake in a preheated oven for 20-22 mins at 200C until crispy. 4. While chicken is still hot, add extra parmesan and parsley. Mix well until coated and extra cheesy. 5. Assemble the wraps with shredded lettuce, onion, tomato, crispy chicken and sauce. ENJOY! Storage and Reheating Tips - Store chicken and creamy sauce in separate containers in the fridge. - When ready to eat, just warm up chicken in oven/air fryer for 4-5 mins 180C / 370F. Warm up sauce in a pan, serve on a wrap with fresh lettuce and enjoy . . . . #garlicparmesan #chickenwrap #chickenrecipes #highprotein #healthyrecipes

101 Steak and Potato Variations Pt. 1: Loaded Steak and Potato Soup 🥔🥣 Comfort food season is in full swing! Gotta add this one to the menu • Ingredients: 3lbs golden potatoes, chopped 16oz steak, any cut you prefer 32 oz (4 cups) low-sodium beef stock (plus more to reach desired soup consistency) 1 medium yellow onion, diced Salt, pepper, garlic (I used Kinder's The Blend) 1lb bacon, cut into small pieces 1 cup shredded Cheddar cheese, divided 4 Tbsp butter 1/4 cup all-purpose flour 12oz evaporated milk Sour cream for topping (optional) 2 Tbsp chives • Instructions -Cook the bacon in a skillet until crisp. Drain and set aside. Reserve a little bacon for topping. -Add the potatoes, beef stock, salt, pepper, garlic to your 5.5-qt slow cooker. -Cook on LOW for 6–7 hours or HIGH for 3–4 hours, until the potatoes are very tender. -About 30 minutes before serving, puree potatoes with an immersion blender. Melt the butter in a saucepan. Whisk in the flour and cook for 1–2 minutes. -Slowly whisk in the evaporated milk until smooth and slightly thickened. -Stir the cream mixture into the slow cooker and add 3/4 of the cooked bacon, 1/2 cup of the cheddar, and the sour cream. Stir gently. -Cook another 20–30 minutes on LOW. During that time, cook the steak and cut it into small pieces. -Serve topped with the remaining cheddar, bacon, chopped steak, and chives.

Ingredients:  • 3 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs, cut into bite-size pieces  • ½ tbsp garlic salt  • 1 tbsp black pepper  • ¼ cup cornstarch (plus a little extra if you want more crunch)  • 2–3 tbsp vegetable oil (for frying) Sauce:  • ½ cup honey  • ¼ cup soy sauce  • 1 tbsp ginger paste  • 2–3 tbsp minced garlic To Finish:  • Sesame seeds  • Green onions, sliced ⸻ Instructions:  1. Recipe👇🏽 Nashville Hot Mozzarella Sticks Just Got Crispier🌶️🔥 These mozzarella sticks just got a serious upgrade. Double-breaded, fried until golden and crispy, then tossed in a Nashville hot oil that brings the heat. Mozzarella Sticks 3 rectangles low-moisture mozzarella, sliced into ½–1 inch sticks Flour, for dusting 2 eggs, beaten 1½ cups breadcrumbs Oil, for frying Nashville Hot Oil ½ cup hot frying oil 2 tbsp cayenne 1 tsp paprika 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tbsp brown sugar Slice the low-moisture mozzarella into ½–1 inch sticks and lightly dust them in flour. Freeze for 1 hour. Dip the frozen mozzarella into the egg, then breadcrumbs, then back into the egg and breadcrumbs again. Heat your oil to 350°F and fry the mozzarella straight from frozen for 2–3 minutes, until golden and crispy. You’ll know they’re ready when they float to the top and look nice and puffy. Don’t overcrowd the pan. While they’re frying, mix the Nashville hot oil ingredients together. As soon as the mozzarella sticks come out, brush or toss them in the hot oil while they’re still steaming. Serve immediately with ranch. I hope it crunches.

One-Pan Chicken Shawarma Rice Bowls 🔥 All the shawarma flavor, none of the extra steps… juicy spiced chicken, onion rice pilaf, refreshing salad and a creamy garlic sauce 🤌 For the Chicken: -1.5 lbs (680g) boneless, skinless chicken thighs -Seasoning: 1 tbsp paprika, 1 tbsp cumin, 1 tbsp onion powder, 2 tsp coriander, 1 tsp allspice, 2 tsp turmeric, 2 tsp pepper, 1 tsp salt -3 tbsp olive oil + 8 garlic cloves -½ lemon, juiced -2 tsp bouillon (I used the roasted chicken base from @Better Than Bouillon) For the Rice: -3 tbsp butter + 1 ½ cups yellow onion, diced -1 tbsp turmeric, 2 tsp paprika, 2 tsp garlic powder, 2 tsp pepper -1 ½ cups basmati rice -3 cups hot water  -3 tsp bouillon  For the Fresh Sumac Salad: -½ large red onion, thinly sliced -1 cup cherry tomatoes, quartered -1 cup cucumber, sliced then halved -1 tsp salt, 1 tsp black pepper & 2 tsp sumac -½ lemon, juiced For the Garlic Sauce: -¼ cup mayonnaise + ¼ cup plain Greek yogurt -2 to 3 garlic cloves + 1 tbsp fresh parsley -1 tsp salt + 1 tsp black pepper -½ lemon, juiced + 1 tbsp olive oil 1. In a bowl, combine the chicken with the spices, olive oil, garlic, lemon juice and bouillon. Mix well. Marinate for as long as your patience can handle. 2. Heat a large pan over medium-high heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Once hot, add the chicken in batches. Cook for 6 to 8 mins per side until golden and cooked through. Set aside. 3. Reduce heat to medium-low. Add butter to the same pan then the onions & cook, stirring often, until translucent. Add the garlic & spices, cook for 1 to 2 mins. Add the rice and toast for 2 mins while stirring. Pour in the hot water mixed with bouillon according to package instructions. Stir & bring to a boil. Once boiling, cover & reduce heat to low. Simmer for 20 mins until cooked. 4. Mix the salad ingredients in one bowl and the sauce ingredients in another bowl. Arsenio’s Chipotle Mac n Cheese Balls 🧀 Recipe👇🏽 Ingredients ½ lb (227 g) cavatappi pasta ¼ cup (57 g) butter ⅓ cup (40–45 g) all-purpose flour 1½ cups (360 ml) milk 1 tsp garlic powder 1 tsp paprika ½ tsp black pepper ¼ chicken bouillon cube, grated 1 tbsp chipotle pepper sauce 1 cup (100 g) shredded marble cheese 1 cup (100 g) shredded mozzarella 1 cup (100 g) extra shredded mozzarella for binding Salt to taste, if needed 2 eggs, beaten Panko breadcrumbs Oil for frying Instructions Cook the cavatappi in salted water until al dente, then drain well. Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic powder, paprika and black pepper, then stir in the flour. Cook for 1–2 minutes, stirring constantly. Turn off the heat, add the marble cheese and mozzarella, and stir until melted. Taste and add salt if needed. Mix the cooked pasta into the cheese sauce until everything is coated. Add the extra 1 cup of shredded mozzarella and mix until combined. Scoop portions onto pieces of parchment paper. Wrap the parchment around each portion and twist the ends to form tight balls. Place on a tray and freeze for about 1 hour, or until firm. Dip each ball into the beaten eggs, then coat generously in panko breadcrumbs. Heat the oil to 350°F (175°C). Fry until golden and crispy, making sure the centres are heated through. Larger balls may need extra time, so test one first. Transfer to a wire rack to drain. DUMP & BAKE SMOTHERED CHICKEN DINNER 🍗🤎 The kind of dinner that tastes like you spent all day in the kitchen, but really you just threw everything in a baking dish and let the oven do the work! Tender, juicy chicken smothered in homemade gravy with hardly any effort. Serve it over mashed potatoes or rice with your favorite sides and you’ve got yourself a good home-cooked meal! RECIPE BELOW ⬇️ Ingredients: 2 lbs boneless, skinless chicken thighs Olive oil Salt & pepper Garlic powder Onion powder Paprika Cajun seasoning (optional, for a little kick) 1 sprig fresh rosemary 2 tbsp butter 2 cups chicken broth Carrots or your favorite veggies 2 tbsp cornstarch + 2 tbsp water (use 3 tbsp of each for a thicker gravy) Directions: 1. Preheat oven to 350°F. Add chicken thighs and carrots to a baking dish. Drizzle with olive oil and season generously with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder, paprika, and Cajun seasoning if using. Don’t be shy with the seasonings! This is where all your flavor comes from, so eyeball it and season heavily. 2. Add rosemary, butter, and chicken broth. Cover tightly with foil and bake at 350°F for approximately 50 minutes. 3. Remove from oven and carefully pour just the broth into a separate bowl or measuring cup. 4. Mix 2 tbsp cornstarch with 2 tbsp cold water to make a slurry. If you prefer a thicker gravy, use 3 tbsp cornstarch and 3 tbsp water instead. Stir the slurry into the hot broth until well combined, then pour everything back over the chicken and veggies. 5. Return to the oven uncovered at 400°F for approximately 20 minutes, or until the gravy has thickened and the chicken is tender and fully cooked (165°F internally). Serve over creamy mashed potatoes or rice with green beans, a warm dinner roll, or whatever your heart desires! That’s the beauty of cooking. Grilled Teriyaki Chicken 🔥🍗 Cook Like an Asian Ep 1: Grilled Teriyaki Chicken. Welcome to my series, where I teach you easy Asian recipes so good, your friends will think you’re Asian. 🤙🏽 Sweet, savory, garlicky chicken thighs grilled over charcoal for smoky flavor and a beautiful char. This is the series where I bring the recipes, and you take the credit. 🙌🏽 Ingredients: 2 lb boneless chicken thighs ½ cup shoyu (soy sauce) ½ cup brown sugar 5 garlic cloves, crushed 1 tbsp crushed ginger 1 tbsp sesame oil 1 tbsp rice vinegar 1 tsp mirin Instructions: 1. Mix the shoyu, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and mirin until combined. 2. Reserve ¼ cup of marinade BEFORE adding the raw chicken. Refrigerate separately for brushing during the cook. 3. Place chicken in a zip-top bag and pour in the remaining marinade. Seal, massage to coat, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes or overnight. 4. Fire up your charcoal grill. Once the coals are hot, keep one side cooler so you can move the chicken if it browns too quickly.  5. Remove chicken from the bag and discard the used marinade. Grill over the hot coals, flipping and brushing both sides with the reserved marinade to build that beautiful char. 6. Move to the cooler side as needed to prevent burning, and cook until the thickest part reaches 165°F. 7. Rest for 5 minutes, then slice and serve with hot rice! 🍚 Don’t let these ingredients intimidate you because I got all of them from my local Walmart! #teriyakichicken #asianfood #easyrecipe

You already know this Cowboy Mashed Potato Casserole is gonna be GOOD! 🤠 To get the recipe, click the link in @allrecipes bio or continue reading! ⬇️ Ingredients: cooking spray 6 strips bacon 2 pounds baking potatoes, peeled and chopped 1 (5 ounce) can evaporated milk or whole milk 2 tablespoons butter 1 1/2 teaspoons salt, divided 1/2 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, divided 1 pound ground beef 1 cup chopped onion 1 green bell pepper, chopped 1 cup frozen whole kernel corn 2 cloves garlic, minced 1 1/2 teaspoons smoked paprika 1/4 cup barbecue sauce 1 tablespoon Worcestershire sauce 1 teaspoon Dijon mustard 1/2 cup shredded Cheddar or pepper Jack cheese 1/4 cup canned French fried onions 2 tablespoons finely chopped fresh parsley Directions: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F. Grease a 2-quart baking dish with cooking spray. Place dish on a baking sheet. Cook bacon in a large skillet over medium, turning occasionally, until crisp, about 10 minutes. Place bacon on a paper towel to drain. Drain all but 1 Tbsp of bacon fat in the skillet. Chop bacon when cool enough to handle. Meanwhile, bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Add potatoes and return to a boil. Cook, covered, until potatoes are fork tender, 15-20 minutes. Drain potatoes. Return potatoes back to the pot along with evaporated milk, butter, 1/2 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Mash potatoes with a potato masher until smooth. Stir 1/4 c chopped bacon into mashed potatoes. Add ground beef, onion, and bell pepper to the skillet with reserved bacon fat. Cook over medium until meat is browned and cooked through, stirring occasionally, 8-10 minutes. Add corn kernels, garlic, and paprika to the skillet. Cook and stir for 1 minute. Stir in barbecue sauce, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, remaining 1 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Spread ground beef mixture in prepared baking dish. Spread potatoes evenly over beef. Sprinkle with cheese, remaining bacon, and French fried onions. Bake until bubbly and cheese is melted, 20-25 minutes. Garnish with parsley. 👨‍🍳: Nicole McLaughlin #cowboycasserole #mashedpotatoes #easydinners #dinnerideas

How to Make Sticky Toffee Pudding 🇬🇧🍨  FULL RECIPE BELOW ⬇️  (feeds 6 people) INGREDIENTS: Pudding ⬇️ 225g pitted dates (~250g unpitted) 1 + 3/4 cups AP flour 1/2 cup boiling water  2 teabags earl grey  1/2 cup milk, at room temperature  2/3 cup + 1 tbsp unsalted butter, softened 2/3 cup brown sugar 2 eggs, at room temperature  2 tbsp molasses 2 tsp vanilla extract  1 tsp baking soda 1.5 tsp baking powder 1 tsp fine salt Toffee Sauce ⬇️ 1 cup brown sugar 1 cup heavy cream 1/2 cup unsalted butter 2 tsp molasses  To Finish ⬇️ Flaky salt (to taste) 1 pint vanilla ice cream INSTRUCTIONS: 1. Pre-heat your oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.  2. Bring your water to a boil. If you’d like to try some date-earl gray tea as well, add an extra cup of boiling water (it was actually quite delicious!) 3. Remove the pits from your dates if you haven’t already. Roughly chop your dates, and add them to a heat-proof container. Pour the boiling water over your dates, and add your tea bags. Let the tea steep for 5 minutes, then remove your tea bags. Remove your tea to drink if you added some extra, leaving only a 1/2 cup of hot water to submerge the dates. Add your 1 tbsp of baking soda, and mix it in with the dates (the mixture should start to foam). Let sit for another 5 minutes. 4. While still warm, blend your date mixture with an immersion blender, and set aside to cool to room temperature. In a large mixing bowl, add 2/3 cup of softened butter. Mix with a hand mixer until the butter is smooth & spread around the bottom of the bowl. Add your brown sugar, and mix once more until the butter & sugar are homogeneous, and have increased in volume (~2 minutes). Each time you mix in a new ingredient, be sure to scrape down the sides of the bowl. One at a time, add your eggs and mix them in on low speed (don’t mix too aggressively!) Wait until the first egg is well incorporated before adding the second one. Add your milk, molasses, and vanilla extract to the bowl, and mix once more to combine.  5. Next, grab a spatula and fold in your date purée. Quickly whisk your baking powder & salt into your flour in a separate bowl. Once incorporated, start adding your flour, about 1/2 cup at a time, using a strainer to sift the flour into the bowl (this will remove any clumps). Ensure each 1/2 cup of flour is well incorporated before adding the next.  6. Grease 6 4.5oz ramekins with your remaining tbsp of softened butter, ensuring they are very well coated. You do not want your STPs to stick to the ramekins! Evenly divide the batter between the ramekins, ensuring you leave at least 1cm of space below the rim (because the puddings will rise quite a bit when baking). 7. Bake the ramekins for 20-30 minutes, or until a cake tester/toothpick comes out *slightly* moist when inserted in the middle of the pudding (not gooey with batter, but not dry either).  8. While the puddings are baking, make your sauce. Add your butter, cream, brown sugar and molasses to a pot, and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Once at a boil, turn the heat down to low, and cook down your sauce until it has thickened & darkened in colour. You will know it’s done when the bubbles on the surface of the sauce are very small (because most of the moisture has already boiled away). Remove your sauce from the burner, but keep in a warm place.  RECIPE CONTINUES IN THE COMMENTS ⬇️ #stp #stickytoffeepudding #dessert #homecooking #recipe

Creamy Tuscan White Beans Ingredients (4-5 servings): • 2 (15-oz) cans white beans, Great Northern or cannellini, drained and rinsed • 1½ cups cherry tomatoes, halved • ⅓ cup sun-dried tomatoes, chopped • 1 small yellow onion, finely diced • 4 garlic cloves, finely minced • 1 tbsp olive oil • 1 tsp Italian seasoning • ½ tsp smoked paprika • ¼ tsp red pepper flakes, plus more to taste • 1 tbsp all-purpose flour • 1½ cups broth • ½ cup whole milk • 1 tsp Dijon mustard • ½ cup finely grated Parmesan, plus more for serving • 2–3 cups chopped kale, tough stems removed • 1 tbsp lemon juice • 1 tsp honey • ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper • Salt, to taste • Extra-virgin olive oil, for finishing • Crusty sourdough, for serving Instructions: 1. Heat a skillet over medium heat. Add the olive oil and diced onion with a pinch of salt. Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until softened and lightly golden. 2. Add the halved cherry tomatoes and cook for 3-4 minutes, stirring occasionally, until they’re blistered and beginning to collapse. Reserve some of the blistered tomatoes for later. 3. Add garlic and sun-dried tomatoes. Cook for 30-60 seconds until fragrant.  4. Stir in Italian seasoning, smoked paprika, red pepper flakes and black pepper. 5. Sprinkle flour over everything and stir for about 30 seconds. Slowly pour in the broth while stirring, followed by the milk and Dijon mustard. 6. Bring to a gentle simmer and cook for 2–3 minutes, stirring, until slightly thickened. 7. Stir in the beans and simmer gently for 5–7 minutes.  8. Mash about ⅓ of the beans against the side of the skillet with the back of a spoon. 9. Stir in the chopped kale, cover, and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring once or twice, until tender but still vibrant. 10. Lower the heat and stir in the Parmesan until melted and glossy. 11. Add lemon juice and honey. Taste and adjust salt, pepper and red pepper flakes. If the sauce is thicker than you want, stir in a splash of broth. 12. Top with the reserved blistered tomatoes, Parmesan, black pepper and a drizzle of olive oil. Enjoy! #beans #whitebeans #fallrecipes #easydinner #dinneridea

Recipe Name Sweet and Smoky Honey Garlic Glazed Pork Tenderloin Ingredients 1. Pork tenderloin – 2 lb 2. Olive oil – 2 tbsp 3. Salt – 1 tsp 4. Black pepper – 1 tsp 5. Smoked paprika – 2 tsp 6. Garlic powder – 1 tsp 7. Onion powder – 1 tsp 8. Dried thyme – 1 tsp 9. Unsalted butter – 2 tbsp 10. Garlic – 5 cloves, minced 11. Honey – 1/3 cup 12. BBQ sauce – 1/2 cup 13. Soy sauce – 2 tbsp 14. Apple cider vinegar – 1 tbsp 15. Dijon mustard – 1 tbsp 16. Brown sugar – 2 tbsp 17. Red pepper flakes – 1/4 tsp, optional 18. Fresh parsley – 1 tbsp, chopped Recipe 1. Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Remove the pork tenderloin from its packaging, trim away excess silver skin, and pat it completely dry with paper towels. 2. In a small bowl, combine the salt, black pepper, smoked paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, and dried thyme. Rub the pork with olive oil, then coat every side evenly with the seasoning mixture. 3. Heat a large oven-safe skillet over medium-high heat. Add a little olive oil if necessary and sear the tenderloin for 2–3 minutes per side until a deep golden-brown crust forms. 4. Transfer the seared pork to a plate temporarily. Reduce the heat to medium and add the butter to the same skillet, allowing it to melt while collecting the flavorful browned bits from the bottom. 5. Add the minced garlic and cook for approximately 30–45 seconds, stirring continuously until fragrant. Avoid browning the garlic too much, as it can become bitter. 6. Stir in the honey, BBQ sauce, soy sauce, apple cider vinegar, Dijon mustard, brown sugar, and optional red pepper flakes. Whisk thoroughly until the ingredients form a smooth, glossy glaze. 7. Simmer the glaze for 2–3 minutes, stirring frequently until slightly thickened. Reserve a few tablespoons of the glaze in a separate clean bowl for brushing on the pork later. 8. Return the pork tenderloin to the skillet and turn it several times to coat it generously with the honey garlic glaze. Spoon additional sauce over the top to ensure an even coating. 9. Transfer the skillet to the preheated oven and roast for approximately 15–25 minutes, depending on the thickness of the tenderloin. Baste the pork with the pan juices halfway through cooking to develop a rich, sticky exterior. 10. Check the thickest part of the tenderloin with a meat thermometer. Remove it when the internal temperature reaches 145°F (63°C), followed by a 3-minute rest for safe, juicy pork. 11. For a darker, caramelized finish, brush the reserved glaze over the tenderloin during the final few minutes of cooking. Broil briefly if desired, watching closely to prevent the honey from burning. 12. Transfer the pork to a cutting board and let it rest for 5–10 minutes so the juices redistribute throughout the meat. Spoon the warm pan glaze over the top before slicing. 13. Slice the tenderloin into thick medallions using a sharp knife. Arrange them on a serving platter, drizzle with the remaining glaze, and garnish with freshly chopped parsley. 14. Serve warm with roasted potatoes, steamed green beans, buttered corn, or creamy mashed potatoes. Spoon extra honey garlic sauce over each serving for a delicious sweet, smoky, and savory finish.
